title: Gideon and the Kitchen
premise: Sebastian Dravenmoor inherited Hollowmere Vineyard along with its crushing debts, and he intends to sell the orchard parcel to a developer to survive the season. But the deed reveals a co-owner: Maren Gideon, the woman who vanished from his life eleven years ago after testifying against his father in an embezzlement trial. Forced into uneasy partnership, they must restore the orchard's failing harvest within one growing cycle or lose everything to the bank. As old wounds reopen, Sebastian learns his father framed Maren, and she learns Sebastian spent years quietly paying her debts out of guilt. In the end they choose each other over the vineyard, selling Hollowmere to the community that worked it and keeping only the orchard—and each other.
about_author: Ivo Nakamura is the pen name of a former sommelier turned novelist who spent a decade working harvests across three continents before writing about love in places where labor and memory intertwine. They live near a defunct orchard they helped save from developers.

chapters.title: The Deed of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Facing foreclosure, Sebastian finds the orchard deed lists a second name: Maren Gideon. The shock of her name after eleven years unsettles him more than the debt does. Emotional beat: dread laced with involuntary hope.

chapters.title: A Woman Named Winter
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren returns to Hollowmere intending only to sign away her share, but the sight of the orchard—where her mother once worked—stalls her resolve. She meets Sebastian at the gate; neither says what needs saying. Emotional beat: guarded grief.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Their lawyer forces a compromise: joint ownership means joint decisions, and the bank gives them until harvest to prove solvency. Sebastian proposes restoring the orchard together; Maren agrees with visible reluctance. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: Pruning What Remains
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. First days of shared work. Maren discovers Sebastian knows her mother's pruning techniques—a detail that shouldn't be possible unless he studied them. Emotional beat: suspicion softening into curiosity.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A creditor arrives demanding payment; Sebastian hides how deep the debts run. He recalls the trial where Maren testified, and the letter he never sent her. Emotional beat: guilt compounding like interest.

chapters.title: The Kitchen at Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Rain traps them in the estate kitchen, where Maren once ate as a child alongside Sebastian's family. Old memories surface between chopping apples; for one evening, the past tense slips. Emotional beat: warmth breaking through armor.

chapters.title: Blight
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Disease strikes half the orchard. The developer, Corvane, makes a tempting early offer, and Sebastian is tempted—until he sees Maren's face when she reads the contract. Emotional beat: temptation versus loyalty.

chapters.title: What the Trial Never Said
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren confesses why she testified: she was coerced, threatened with her mother's pension. She never told Sebastian because she believed he'd hate her either way. Emotional beat: confession without absolution.

chapters.title: Eleven Years of Interest
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Rummaging through his father's papers for loan documents, Sebastian finds proof his father orchestrated the embezzlement and framed Maren. He sits with the truth all night, unable to tell her. Emotional beat: horror and paralysis.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Desperate for pickers, they hire the town's seasonal workers, many of whom remember Maren's mother. The community rallies around the orchard, and Maren feels roots regrowing. Emotional beat: belonging rediscovered.

chapters.title: Corvane's Second Letter
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Corvane raises the offer and hints he knows about Maren's coerced testimony, threatening exposure if the sale falls through. Sebastian realizes someone fed Corvane information from inside. Emotional beat: paranoia tightening.

chapters.title: The Mirror Argument
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. After finding Sebastian's hidden ledger showing payments made anonymously to her over the years, Maren confronts him. The fight turns intimate—both accusing the other of choosing silence over love. Emotional beat: rupture.

chapters.title: Frost Warning
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. An unseasonal frost threatens the crop on the eve of the bank inspection. Sebastian works through the night lighting smudge pots alone, too proud to wake her. Emotional beat: solitary devotion.

chapters.title: Smoke at Dawn
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren wakes, sees the fires, and joins him without a word. Working shoulder to shoulder through dawn, they save most of the crop. Neither apologizes yet, but something mends. Emotional beat: reconciliation without words.

chapters.title: The Father's Ghost
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian finally tells Maren the truth about his father's frame-up, producing the letters as evidence. Her reaction isn't relief but fury—at him for carrying it alone. Emotional beat: truth as both wound and salve.

chapters.title: What Justice Costs
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren wants to expose the dead man publicly; Sebastian wants to bury it forever. Their definitions of justice collide, echoing the theme that the law failed them both. Emotional beat: moral standoff.

chapters.title: Corvane Moves
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Corvane files a fraudulent lien to force the sale, revealing his informant: the estate's longtime accountant, complicit in the original embezzlement. The threat becomes concrete and immediate. Emotional beat: siege mentality.

chapters.title: The Town That Kept Receipts
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren turns to the harvest workers and townsfolk, gathering testimony and records proving the orchard's true ownership history. Justice outside the law takes shape as collective memory. Emotional beat: empowerment through community.

chapters.title: Climax: The Auction Room
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the forced auction, Maren presents the evidence—the forged deed chain, the accountant's confession—while Sebastian publicly renounces his inheritance claim so the community can bid. Corvane collapses; the lien dissolves. Emotional beat: vindication earned together.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Apples
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The town buys Hollowmere collectively; Sebastian and Maren retain only the orchard. Exhausted and broke but free, they sort the harvest in the kitchen, laughing for the first time. Emotional beat: lightness after weight.

chapters.title: Present Tense
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Sebastian finally sends the eleven-year-old letter, unread, then writes a new one by hand. He asks Maren to stay not as co-owner but as partner. She answers by planting a new tree with him. Emotional beat: love chosen openly.

chapters.title: Gideon and the Kitchen
chapters.summary: Dual POV, epilogue. One year later: first press of their own cider in the rebuilt kitchen, the community gathered, Maren's mother's name carved above the door. Memory honored, justice done, love in present tense. Emotional beat: quiet, earned joy.
